text:
Utah arrives in Las Vegas on a slide, having lost 4-2 at Ottawa four days ago and gone 2-2-1 in its last five while being outscored 20-16. The Mammoth are also thin on the back end and up front, without Kailer Yamamoto and John Marino, with Nate Schmidt also out. Vegas has won three straight, most recently 4-1 at Buffalo, though Noah Hanifin and Parker Wotherspoon are missing. It's also a rematch of last spring's first-round series, which the Golden Knights won in six. That storyline isn't in our numbers, so we wouldn't lean on it.

In expected goals (the quality of shots taken and allowed), Utah has the better season, with 58% of the five-on-five share against Vegas's 52%. But the Golden Knights' three straight wins are only half backed by the chances, 49% of the expected goals, with goaltending doing a lot of the work. Our model has it close: VGK 3.22 expected goals, UTA 3.01. Vegas's penalty kill allows 0.49 expected goals a game to Utah's 0.68, and Utah takes 4.3 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Sebastian Cossa is at -3.4 goals saved above expected (how many more or fewer goals a goalie stops than the shots deserved) over seven games. Carter Hart, also projected, is at +2.1 this season after -4.4 last year.

For Utah, Logan Cooley has 13 points in 10 games and scores in 33% of our simulations, though our numbers say he's due to cool. For Vegas, Jack Eichel has a 37% chance at two or more points, and Mark Stone leads the Golden Knights at 35% to score.
